increment_paragraph: **P0-G1-CLOSURE-RECORD** (round 41; USER DECISION 2026-11-27: "the G1 closure record and CONNECT-LIBC-EFFECT-CLAIMS are still open. We need to launch this card"; [report](../../reports/g1-closure-record/README.md)). No analyzer, contract or gateway semantic change. REEVALUATION_SPEC §9's gate G1 (certificate containment) is evaluated against its deliverable and criterion, and is **met within a stated scope**. The criterion is 16 formulas over a new records vocabulary, the `G1` block of the C04.18.9 typed rendering (`g1_`-prefixed; sorts `g1_finding` and `g1_case`; no premise formula, contract or analyzer reads it, and it has no Lean model). Every formula is checked by `guarded_proposition` and decided over the record's 27-row case table (`crates/qcore-frontend/tests/g1_closure_formulas.rs`). For each of WM01, WM02, WM03, VP01 and VP02 there is an executed negative control (the probe entry plus its regression tests), an executed positive control and an executed profile control. The profile controls are the atomic source route's refusals for WM, and QP005 or QP001 for VP. The eight profile restrictions in force (R-WM1 to R-WM3, R-VP1 to R-VP5) each fail closed. The first-party manifests' wildcard targets are not relied upon: protocol v1 issues no certificate in any profile. Scope: `C11ExecutionCertificate` for one supplied graph in the N1570 atomic fragment, and `CoreCertificate` from `verify` (v1, none issuable) and `verify_v2` (only through a registered trusted-core replay of a non-empty core inventory; ResourceContracts, ChunkLifecycle, ObservationHooks). Two firewall controls were added to `crates/qcore-verifier-host/tests/plugin_firewall.rs`. The first is the v2 empty-core-inventory refusal (QP016). It had no test, and with the guard disabled it mints `Safe`. The second covers an unmatched target or capability (QP005). Both examples exit 0 (`reevaluation_probe` 8 probes, `reevaluation_followup` 11, `failed_expectations` 0). Excluded and registered: capabilities without a core checker, legitimate empty scopes, the WM certificate's model identity, a mixed-size control at the atomic route. Third-party `Unsafe` validation stays with W45-PLUGIN-COUNTEREXAMPLE-CHECKER. G2-G6 are untouched. §9 carries a one-sentence pointer.

ledger.why: Discharged by P0-G1-CLOSURE-RECORD (docs/reports/g1-closure-record/README.md, base 9903b027a). The record evaluates REEVALUATION_SPEC §9's G1 deliverable and criterion per finding, as 16 validator-checked formulas over the G1 block decided over a 27-row case table. G1 is met within its scope: C11ExecutionCertificate for one supplied graph in the N1570 atomic fragment, and CoreCertificate from verify (v1: none issuable) and verify_v2 (registered trusted-core replay of a non-empty core inventory; ResourceContracts, ChunkLifecycle, ObservationHooks). Every finding has an executed negative, positive and profile control, and the eight profile restrictions in force fail closed. Both reevaluation examples exit 0. The open items it excludes are listed and tracked: G1-EXCLUDED-CAPABILITIES-WITHOUT-CHECKER, G1-EXCLUDED-EMPTY-SCOPE-ARGUMENT, G1-WM-CERTIFICATE-MODEL-IDENTITY, G1-WM-MIXED-SIZE-ROUTE-CONTROL and W45-PLUGIN-COUNTEREXAMPLE-CHECKER.

ledger.title: EventTraces, Concurrency and TranslationUnitProjection have no core witness checker, so no certificate exists for them
ledger.text: P0-G1-CLOSURE-RECORD: G1's closure covers CoreCertificates only for capabilities with a registered trusted-core WitnessChecker (ResourceContracts, ChunkLifecycle, ObservationHooks). Every v2 request for EventTraces, Concurrency or TranslationUnitProjection is Unknown (QP016, check_evidence_v2), and every v1 request is Unknown (QP009, check_evidence). That is containment, not verification. REEVALUATION_SPEC §6 and §9 G2 require a versioned capability-specific relation check(program, profile, assumptions, witness) with a proof that an accepted witness entails the property. DISCHARGE: a trusted-core checker per capability with its core-derived inventory, a positive and a negative control through verify_v2, and Lean parity; or a recorded decision that the capability stays uncertifiable.

ledger.title: A genuinely empty verification scope cannot be certified: no independently checked no-obligations argument exists
ledger.text: P0-G1-CLOSURE-RECORD: VP02's containment refuses every empty scope. v1 refuses empty facts, claims or coverage (QP009, check_evidence). v2 refuses an empty core inventory (QP016, check_evidence_v2, tested by g1_vp02_empty_core_inventory_cannot_obtain_a_v2_certificate). A scope that truly has no obligations is therefore Unknown, a precision gap rather than a containment gap. REEVALUATION_SPEC §6: an empty scope is safe only with an independently checked no-obligations argument. DISCHARGE: a core-derived, independently checked no-obligations argument, with a control showing that it certifies a genuinely empty scope and refuses a provider-asserted one; or a recorded decision that empty scopes stay Unknown.

ledger.title: C11ExecutionCertificate names no memory model or semantic profile
ledger.text: P0-G1-CLOSURE-RECORD: the weak-memory checker admits exactly one model, C11 as published (N1570), atomic fragment, with no model parameter (R-WM1). G1's profile restriction therefore holds by construction. But the certificate value check_c11_execution returns (crates/qcore-core/src/weak_memory.rs: event_count, happens_before, source_observation) carries no model, standard or fragment identifier. REEVALUATION_SPEC §1 requires every published result to identify its semantic profile, and §2 says to select the same model before comparing verdicts. DISCHARGE: carry the model identity (standard, fragment, checker version) on the certificate and on every verdict built on it, with a test; or show that each publishing consumer already names it.

ledger.title: No executed control shows that the atomic source route refuses a mixed-size, union or bit-field access to an atomic object
ledger.text: P0-G1-CLOSURE-RECORD: mixed-size accesses are outside the weak-memory model (no MemoryEventKind), so they cannot reach check_c11_execution directly. G1's record executed the atomic route's refusals for consume, __sync, by-pointer, unlisted and unevaluated forms (cg19_refusals_name_the_form_and_card). It executed no case in which C source accesses an atomic object through a differently sized or overlapping lvalue (a union arm, a char pointer, a bit-field). REEVALUATION_SPEC §2 (Marmanis et al.) requires unsupported mixed-size behaviour to remain Unknown. DISCHARGE: a source-level control per shape showing a refusal (Unknown) and never a represented event, or a fix where one is admitted.
